outlier.evidence: Ratings 7/7/6/6 span one point. The two 7s are the least grounded: Reviewer_6RBj says it is 'not comfortable enough with the theory here to spot non-obvious mistakes', and Reviewer_u8GD raises only two clarity points. The 6s come from the two reviewers who spent 10-11 hours (Reviewer_eRAu, Reviewer_6XLT).

inattentive_reviews.evidence: A 7 at confidence 3 after 4 hours. The review raises the optimizer in Theorem 1, an empirical check of the variance-mean ratio, and a notation nit. It says nothing about the one-action restriction, the supervised setting or the tie to model-based RL, which every other reviewer in both committees discussed. Its post-rebuttal note is 'Thanks for the clarifications.'

checkable_claims.claim: The paper says its results for the explicit parameterization are not novel (line 189).
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 189-190: 'this result isn't novel and follows from standard results of convex optimization [3], but is stated here to facilitate comparisons'. The authors replied that only the implicit-parameterization results are contributions.

checkable_claims.claim: The Conclusion asserts that the results may generalize to full MDPs without evidence.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 345-350 give only an informal argument: the Bellman-optimality subderivatives depend on the chain induced by the optimal policy. The submission has no proof or experiment for the MDP case; the 4-action runs appeared only in the rebuttal.

checkable_claims.claim: Theorem 1 does not say which optimizer produces the implicit sequence.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 131-135 say the explicit weights come from gradient descent but the implicit ones are 'obtained by optimizing L(g_implicit(w,F))', linked only by 'similarly'. The theorem statement (lines 141-142) names no optimizer. The authors promised to state (S)GD.

checkable_claims.claim: Both parameterizations reach the same optimum when X has full rank, so the gaps in the experiments must come from stopping SGD early.
checkable_claims.evidence: The global-convergence results (Corollaries 1-2) imply the same limiting weights. The authors confirmed 'we run each method for a fixed number of updates'. The main text (lines 274-281) gives no update count, and Figure 2 reports only the 'final residual'.

checkable_claims.claim: Typos in the appendix proofs: U for A in (48)-(49), an extra phi in (87), a reused index in (106), and r_max not squared in the proof of Corollary 4.
checkable_claims.evidence: The proofs are in the supplement, which is not part of the 11-page submitted PDF. The authors conceded every item.

rebuttal.evidence: Reviewer_6XLT edited 2021-09-02 and wrote 'I have updated my score on the basis of this response'; the final 6 means it rose from 5 or below. Reviewer_6RBj (edit 2021-08-30) added 'inclined to keep my current score'. Reviewer_u8GD (edit 2021-08-29) added only 'Thanks for the clarifications'. Reviewer_eRAu wrote on 2021-09-01 'I'm inclined to maintain my score' and never edited.
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: 6XLT accepted a point-by-point reply: Markov-reward-chain gradients match MDP gradients under the optimal policy, a 4-action sanity check gave qualitatively similar results, VIN-style methods differ from classical model-based RL, and all implicit-parameterization results are new. 6XLT still asked for a discussion of the simplifying assumptions and of which model-based variant the paper means.

ac.evidence: Three-sentence meta-review: 'after the author response, all of the reviewers agree that the theoretical results while limited in some ways are interesting and significant enough for acceptance.' It adds 6XLT's request for a balanced discussion of the full-MDP case. It shows no reading of its own.

main_reasons_for_decision: All four reviewers ended above threshold (7/7/6/6) after the rebuttal
Global convergence despite non-convexity and the preconditioning view judged novel and interesting as a first theoretical step
One internal action and the supervised setting accepted as fair simplifications for theory (6RBj, eRAu)
The rebuttal's 4-action sanity check and novelty statement moved 6XLT to 6

outlier.evidence: Ratings 3/3/4/5/5/6 spread evenly with no isolated value. The lone 6 (Reviewer_AqM3) is at confidence 2 and admits 'no prior experience in working with gradient descent dynamics'. The two 3s (Reviewer_kLUp, Reviewer_EkYa) carry the committee's highest confidence, 4.

inattentive_reviews.evidence: Spent 20 hours but misread the setup. It doubts that g reaches every weight vector, but line 140 gives theta_hat = A^{-1} w with w free. It says data sampling is not discussed and asks whether the data change over time, but line 127 fixes a dataset D and lines 265-271 describe offline rollouts. It says the Markov reward chain has no formal definition, but lines 80-82 define it as an MDP with a singleton action.

The committee's only above-threshold rating rests on proofs it says it has 'not checked ... carefully' and on generic praise ('the derivation is smooth and has good logic flow'). Confidence 2; the post-rebuttal note is 'my review keeps the same'.

checkable_claims.claim: Corollary 3 is wrong: sum r_i^2 should not cancel with ||sum r_i phi(x_i)||^2, so both parameterizations should have the same variance-mean ratio.
checkable_claims.evidence: With one-hot features and one datapoint per state, ||sum_i r_i e_i||^2 = sum_i r_i^2, and Theorem 5's explicit ratio reduces to n(k-1)/(k(n-1)) + (n-k)n/(k(n-1)) = n/k. LFGm withdrew the claim on 2021-08-15. Corollary 3 (lines 241-244) does not state the one-datapoint-per-state condition, and the experiments contain duplicate states (line 271).

checkable_claims.claim: Theorem 4's speed-up compares the convergence of the residual's 1-component with the convergence of the whole loss in Theorems 2-3.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 217-220 compare O(1/(1-eta)^2) for the 1-component with O(1/n) for the loss; lines 259-261 call the implicit case 'roughly n times faster'. No explicit-parameterization rate along the 1 direction is derived. The authors conceded that little can be said when the residual has no 1-component.

checkable_claims.claim: theta_hat = (I - eta sigma(F))^{-1} w has a closed form, so implicit differentiation is unnecessary (also LFGm, issue 6).
checkable_claims.evidence: Line 140 writes theta_hat = A^{-1} w explicitly, yet lines 98-99 claim the implicit form avoids 'needing to consider the algorithm used to compute theta_hat'.

checkable_claims.claim: The abstract states global convergence without a condition that the convergence results need.
checkable_claims.evidence: Corollary 1 (line 154) and Corollary 2 (line 176) carry the condition 'If O(alpha^2) <= alpha^2 C for some C >= 0'; abstract lines 9-11 state the result without it. CGbD accepted the authors' reply that the term vanishes at stationary points. The camera-ready restates Corollary 1 for gradient flow and drops the SGD convergence corollary.

checkable_claims.claim: The method has no policy improvement or model-based value-iteration step; it is a reparameterized model-free method.
checkable_claims.evidence: Singleton internal action (line 95); policy evaluation by regression on a fixed dataset (lines 56, 127-128). The authors conceded: 'Both our formulation and value iteration networks should be thought of as model-free methods.'

checkable_claims.claim: With no reward offset, the two parameterizations perform about equally well.
checkable_claims.evidence: Figure 2 at offset 0: chain about 4.9 vs 4.1 with overlapping bands; four rooms about 3 vs 2; mountain car about 390 vs 315 with overlapping bands. A clear gap appears only as the offset grows, and mainly in four rooms.

checkable_claims.claim: The image of g may not cover the weight space, so the proof of Corollary 1 is doubtful.
checkable_claims.evidence: theta_hat = A^{-1} w (line 140) with w unconstrained reaches every vector for any fixed F, because A = I - eta sigma(F) is invertible for eta < 1.

checkable_claims.claim: The paper does not say how datapoints are collected or whether they change over time.
checkable_claims.evidence: Line 127 fixes a dataset D of n points; lines 265-271 describe offline rollouts of a fixed epsilon-greedy policy with Monte Carlo return targets.

checkable_claims.claim: The paper does not consider the computational cost of the implicit gradient.
checkable_claims.evidence: The submission never discusses per-step cost. The authors replied that cost is irrelevant to an analysis of gradient dynamics.

rebuttal.evidence: Reviewer_LFGm edited 2021-08-15: 'After rebuttal, authors clarified my doubts about corollary 3 and I increased my rating to 5.' Reviewer_AqM3 edited 2021-09-02 but wrote 'my review keeps the same'. Reviewer_CGbD (2021-08-12), Reviewer_g4M6 (2021-08-16), Reviewer_kLUp and Reviewer_EkYa (2021-08-19) replied and kept their scores; none of them edited.
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: Technical clarifications landed: the Corollary 3 cancellation (LFGm) and the O(alpha^2) term vanishing at stationary points (CGbD). The framing defence did not. The authors conceded to kLUp and EkYa that the formulation is 'model-free'; EkYa and CGbD then cited kLUp's objection. The 4-action sanity check moved no one. g4M6 rejected the reply on implicit differentiation and asked why this parameterization matters at all. LFGm held that a bias term makes the 1 direction of little relevance.

ac.evidence: Rejects with mean 4.33 and four of six reviewers below threshold. Rests on 'all six reviewers have struggled to find a clear and strong connection' to 'a theoretical account of the performance of end-to-end model-based methods' (the paper's lines 43-44, which CGbD quoted) and on the 'lack of substantial (practical) results'. 'All six' overstates AqM3, who wrote that the paper gives 'some novel insight on the principle of end-to-end model-based RL methods'. The advice to seek 'a more specialist audience' echoes kLUp.

main_reasons_for_decision: Weak link between the analysed setting and the end-to-end model-based methods the paper claims to explain (kLUp, EkYa, CGbD, AC)
Authors conceded the formulation is model-free, with no policy improvement
Simplified setting (one action, fixed-data regression, optimization only) limits significance (LFGm, CGbD, EkYa)
Speed-up rests on the constant residual direction, and without a reward offset the parameterizations perform alike (LFGm, kLUp)
No substantial practical results; value judged to be for a specialist audience (AC, kLUp)

issues_only_a: Which results are novel; the explicit-parameterization results are standard (6XLT)
Both parameterizations share one optimum, so the experiments reflect a fixed update budget (eRAu)
No guidance on choosing the internal discount eta (eRAu)
Empirical check of the variance-mean ratio (u8GD); the authors' new runs showed only a weak effect
issues_only_b: Closed form theta_hat = A^{-1} w makes implicit differentiation unnecessary; no reason to study this over-parameterization over others (g4M6, LFGm)
Theorem 4 rates the residual's 1-component but is compared with whole-loss rates; a bias term, TD or baselines already handle a uniform offset (LFGm, kLUp)
Without a reward offset the two parameterizations perform alike (kLUp)
Abstract states global convergence without the corollaries' O(alpha^2) condition (CGbD)
The analysed method is model-free with no policy improvement, which the authors conceded (kLUp, EkYa)
No learning curves despite convergence-rate claims (LFGm)
Computational cost of the implicit gradient ignored (g4M6)
shared_issues: Restriction to a Markov reward chain (one action) and doubt that results extend to MDPs (6XLT, 6RBj; CGbD, EkYa, LFGm)
Supervised regression on a fixed dataset instead of TD or control (6XLT, 6RBj; LFGm, EkYa)
Unclear relation to VIN and to model-based RL as usually understood (6XLT; kLUp, EkYa, CGbD)
Results cover optimization, not generalization or sample efficiency (eRAu; LFGm)
Experiments only in toy domains (6RBj; AqM3, kLUp)
Typos in the appendix proofs, both citing (106) (eRAu; LFGm)
verdict: The committees weighed the same facts differently, and no reviewer found a fatal error. Both saw the same limits: one internal action, regression on a fixed dataset, linear features, and a loose tie to the end-to-end model-based methods the title names. Committee A treated these as fair simplifications for a first theoretical step. Its sceptic, Reviewer_6XLT, raised the same framing gap as B, treated it as a clarity fix after the rebuttal, and rose to 6. A's two 7s are thin, because neither reviewer checked the maths. Committee B held that the paper does not deliver the 'theoretical account of the performance of end-to-end model-based methods' that lines 43-44 promise. In B's rebuttal the authors conceded that their formulation and VIN 'should be thought of as model-free methods'. Reviewer_kLUp and Reviewer_EkYa, B's two confidence-4 reviewers, kept their 3s, and EkYa and Reviewer_CGbD cited kLUp. B also raised correct points that A never saw: the implicit weights have a closed form, the speed-up rests on the constant residual direction, and without a reward offset the parameterizations perform alike. Both ACs followed their reviewers.
evidence_pointers: Authors' rebuttal to Reviewer_kLUp ('should be thought of as model-free methods')
